summary: Weekend-aware scan of the latest arXiv recent listings found no new Sunday submissions; the strongest relevant papers are concentrated in small-system collectivity, finite-density QCD response, heavy-quark transport, CGC computational phenomenology, and validation/deployment-oriented physics AI/ML.
strongest_paper_summary: CMS arXiv:2608.18256 is the most directly consequential heavy-ion result: a first O-O strange-hadron baryon-to-meson enhancement measurement that constrains how QGP-like hadronization signatures evolve with system size.

papers.title: Observation of enhanced baryon production using strange hadrons in oxygen-oxygen collisions
papers.abstract: CMS measures K0S and Lambda spectra in O-O and pp collisions at 5.36 TeV and reports a pronounced Lambda-to-K0S enhancement in O-O, interpreted as evidence relevant to strangeness, radial flow, coalescence, and possible small-system deconfinement.

papers.title: Correspondence between hydrodynamic frames, transport coefficients, and hydrodynamic modes in relativistic fluids
papers.abstract: Derives transformations between Eckart and Landau-Lifshitz frames and shows sound attenuation remains invariant while thermal conductivity values differ in a baryon-rich relativistic fluid example.

papers.title: Negative diffusion in the Functional Renormalization Group flow for the Quark-Diquark Model
papers.short_authors: Johannes Poeplau; Ashutosh Dash; Dirk H. Rischke
papers.abstract: Identifies negative diffusion in FRG quark-diquark-model flows as a model feature rather than a numerical artifact and proposes hyperdiffusion regularization for high-density phase-diagram studies.

papers.title: The QCD crossover temperature and curvature coefficient from unbiased exponential resummation at physical quark masses in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Applies unbiased exponential resummation to finite-density baryon susceptibilities and obtains pseudocritical temperatures and curvature estimates consistent with earlier Taylor-expansion lattice-QCD results.

papers.title: Heavy quark transport in quark-gluon plasma beyond the non-relativistic limit
papers.short_authors: Krishna Rajagopal; Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld; Urs Achim Wiedemann
papers.abstract: Proposes a heavy-quark transport description that encodes non-Gaussian momentum-transfer distributions rather than relying on quasiparticles or Gaussian diffusion assumptions.

papers.title: Photon bremsstrahlung from heavy quarks in a dense nuclear matter
papers.short_authors: Le Zhang; Shanshan Cao; De-Fu Hou; Guang-You Qin
papers.abstract: Derives medium-induced photon radiation from heavy and light quarks at next-to-leading twist while retaining the exchanged-gluon momentum distribution beyond collinear expansion.

papers.title: Fourier Transforms of Color Glass Condensate Multi-Wilson-Line Correlators via Filon Quadrature
papers.short_authors: Haowu Duan; Si-Wei Dai; Cong Yi; Wenbin Zhao
papers.abstract: Develops and validates Filon-type quadrature and GPU kernels for oscillatory Hankel transforms of CGC multi-Wilson-line correlators, with public code and large runtime improvements.

papers.title: Symbolic Regression for Interpretable Emulation of Proton Collective Flow in Intermediate-Energy Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.short_authors: Nicholas Cox; Xavier Grundler; Bao-An Li
papers.abstract: Builds symbolic-regression emulators for IBUU proton flow observables and inverse relations for in-medium nucleon-nucleon cross-section modification, comparing with DNN emulators.

papers.title: Distilling Normalizing Flows for Real-Time Anomaly Detection at the LHC
papers.short_authors: Tara P. A. Tahseen; Noah Clarke Hall; Nikolaos Konstantinidis; Paula Martinez Suarez
papers.abstract: Distills likelihoods from conditional normalizing flows into lightweight FPGA-suitable decision-tree and neural-network students for low-latency anomaly detection at the LHC.

papers.title: Safe Domain Adaptation for Physics: Overcoming Nuisances, Label Shifts, and Simulation Priors
papers.abstract: Shows that adversarial domain adaptation can import simulation-prior bias under label shifts and proposes adaptive reweighting plus label-free model selection on a physics benchmark.

papers.title: FAST-HEP: Compiling Declarative Analysis Workflows for High-Energy Physics and Beyond
papers.abstract: Presents a declarative workflow language, compiler, and runtime intended to separate scientific analysis descriptions from execution details while preserving validation and provenance.

papers.title: Green BOA: Determining the environmental break-even point for ML-based data compression
papers.short_authors: Caterina Doglioni; Akshat Gupta; Thomas Elliott; Hanzila Hussain; Sanjiban Sengupta
papers.abstract: Estimates environmental break-even points for ML-based lossless compression by comparing training/inference carbon costs with disk-storage savings.
